# CloudWatch

* Collects and manages operational data (any data generated by an environment)
    * Operational data: any data generated by an environment, either detailing how it performs, how it nominally runs or any logging data that it generates 

* Metrics:
    * Allows the collection of metrics, monitoring of metrics and action based on metrics
    * Metrics are data relating to AWS products, applications or on-premises systems
* CloudWatch Logs: 
    * Allows for the collection, monitoring and actions based on logging data. Almost anything which is logged can be ingested
* CloudWatch Events: 
    * This functions as an event hub 
    * If an AWS service does something then CloudWatch Events will generate an event which can perform another action
    * CloudWatch Events can generate an event to do something at a certain time

## Namespace

* A container for monitoring data
* Namespaces have a name
* All AWS data goes into an AWS namespace, which is called AWS/ and the service name

## Metric

* A collection of related data points in a time ordered structure

## Datapoint

* An individual measurement value with a timestamp
* It has two parts: A timestamp (year, month, day, hour, minute, second and time zone), and a Value 

## Dimension

* Sent along with datapoints
* Are name value pairs that allow CloudWatch separate datapoints for different things or perspectives within the same metrics

## Alarms

* Are linked to specific metrics, and based in how they are configured they will take an action based on that metric
